## **Detection and Characterization of Photovoltaic Fault Signatures from Unstructured Field Notes to Support OEM Maintenance Optimization**
Arun Veeramany (arun.veeramany@pnnl.gov), Meghana Ramesh (meghana.ramesh@pnnl.gov)


Faults in photovoltaic (PV) systems can lead to significant losses in energy production and increased operations and maintenance (O\&M) costs, particularly when unplanned truck rolls are required for corrective actions. Early detection and classification of faults enable proactive maintenance, reducing downtime and optimizing operational efficiency. This report presents a data-driven approach to fault detection using machine learning (ML) techniques that integrate operational data, environmental measurements, and unstructured field notes from technician reports. The workflow outlines the systematic process of fault signature extraction and classification, incorporating key stages such as data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model training. Unstructured event descriptions were leveraged to enhance the labeling and identification of distinct fault categories, offering deeper insights into fault patterns and causal relationships. A deployment framework is proposed to facilitate model integration into existing PV maintenance systems, emphasizing configurable sensitivity, feedback mechanisms, and dynamic retraining for continuous operational improvement. The matured ML models were deployed and successfully tested at Ecogy Energy within their AWS ecosystem.
